title: QBR - Orion Analytics Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check to review usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents over the last quarter, open roadmap items, and agree next steps for cost optimization and a planned pilot for Dedicated capacity.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Orion Head of ML), Tom Reed (Eng Manager), Priya Nair (Security Ops)

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone thanks for joining, just to confirm we have about 40 minutes, is that right?
[00:05] Sofia: yep that works for us, thanks Jamie.
[00:12] Jamie: quick agenda, usage & cost, reliability incidents, roadmap asks, security checklist, and next steps — we'll go through the QBR slide deck i sent earlier, feel free to interrupt.
[00:28] Marcus: hey, i'll jump into the performance section after Jamie covers usage.
[00:35] Tom: cool. also we had a couple of follow-ups from the last CSM ticket about cache warmup — will cover that in reliability.

[02:00] Jamie: alright first slide, over the last 90 days you've consumed about 1.3B tokens, embeddings make up ~38% of calls, growth is about 22% q/q, main drivers are increased product recommendations and a new chat assistance feature. cost wise your hosted spend averaged $18k/mo, with spikes during Black Friday test runs.
[02:45] Sofia: ok interesting — the embeddings usage is higher than we thought, is that because of batched re-indexes? we do daily batch jobs yes?
[02:52] Tom: yea we have a nightly reindex that runs with full embeddings for new content, that aligns.
[03:10] Jamie: right, we also flagged some high-cost patterns: many small embedding calls rather than batching, and a few long-generation chat endpoints with max tokens at 2048 which are expensive.
[03:40] Sofia: hmmm that explains the bill. is there an easy config we can change to reduce those generation lengths without impacting UX?
[03:50] Marcus: yes, suggestions — 1) lower max_tokens to 512 for assistant route and rely on streaming; 2) enable prefix KV caching for repeated conversational prefixes; 3) batch embeddings with the batch API and increase concurrency to reduce per-call overhead. we can show a config diff.
[04:15] Priya: on batching, any privacy concerns? nightly jobs contain PII sometimes. we need to ensure data at rest is encrypted and logs aren't storing payloads.
[04:30] Jamie: good call — for hosted we do not persist customer payloads beyond retention window, and we offer field-level redaction in the pipeline. we can share the security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts.

[06:00] (slide turn)
[06:10] Marcus: moving to latency & reliability — median p95 latency on your primary model is 230ms for short chat turns, but there were 3 incidents in March where latency spiked to >2s due to autoscaling backoff caused by a bad model rollout. we recommended a canary with traffic shaping.
[06:35] Tom: yes that outage impacted our support SLAs — we had elevated error rates while the new model warmed up. can you drill into the root cause?
[06:45] Marcus: initial analysis shows the new model variant had a larger KV cache footprint and caused memory pressure on the pool, autoscaler removed nodes due to OOM and then spin-up took extra time. our ops team patched the rollout policy to use slower ramp and fallback to previous variant.
[07:10] Sofia: is there a way to pin a route to Dedicated for critical traffic so we avoid shared-hosted scaling issues?
[07:20] Jamie: yes that's exactly the Dedicated pilot we discussed — reserved capacity would give predictable throughput. cost will be higher fixed monthly but you avoid noisy neighbor scaling hits.

[08:30] Priya: for Dedicated, how does key management work? can we bring our own KMS/HSM?
[08:40] Jamie: yes, BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated via KMS integrations; we also have audit logs and TLS mTLS options for private deployments. we'll include the PKI/KMS integration guide.

[10:00] (customers ask about roadmap)
[10:10] Sofia: roadmap question — we need better model evaluation hooks to detect regressions on production prompts. any roadmap items?
[10:20] Marcus: we're rolling out Redwood Optimize features that let you tie evals and prompt sets to alerts; you can register prompt-based tests and get regression alerts when model outputs deviate on metrics. planned GA Q3.
[10:40] Tom: will that include automated A/B rollouts? we want to run canaries and evaluate quality metrics automatically.
[10:50] Marcus: yes, canary + automated metric checks are in scope — you can set thresholds and rollback rules. we'll provide the rollouts doc.

[12:00] Jamie: switching to costs again — we modeled a Dedicated pilot estimate: for your 100qps peak baseline the 3-card DGX-style pool would be approx $36k/mo reserved (illustrative) with 20% lower per-token variable cost vs hosted.
[12:30] Sofia: ok that's significant. can we start with a hybrid: keep lower priority routes on hosted, and route critical requests to Dedicated?
[12:40] Jamie: absolutely — smart routing supports policy-based routing by route, latency SLO, or cost tiers. we can help define routes.

[14:00] (discussion about instrumentation)
[14:15] Tom: we need better trace correlation between our traces and Redwood request ids to debug latency.
[14:25] Marcus: we emit request-id headers and have trace hooks; we can map those to your tracing with the provided snippet. i'll share an example.

[16:00] (security deep-dive)
[16:10] Priya: compliance quick check — SOC2 in place? data residency for EU?
[16:20] Jamie: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; we support region pinning in EU for hosted and private cloud options for EU-residency. we'll pass the contractual data residency addendum.

[18:00] Sofia: any outstanding technical debt or TODOs from your side?
[18:10] Jamie: we have one open support ticket about cache warmup for your nightly jobs, engineering is scheduled next week to implement a pre-warm hook.

[20:00] (recap & next steps)
[20:10] Jamie: recap — 1) we'll send a granular usage & cost breakdown with per-route recommendations; 2) Marcus will share rollout/canary best practices and the trace integration snippet; 3) we'll share SOC2 and KMS integration guides; 4) you requested a Dedicated pilot estimate and a proposed routing plan.
[20:45] Sofia: sounds good, can we also get a quick runbook for incident playbooks?
[20:52] Marcus: yes, playbooks and rollback steps will be included.
[21:00] Tom: timeline wise, if we want to pilot Dedicated next month what's the lead time?
[21:10] Jamie: typical lead is 2–4 weeks for provisioning and onboarding for Dedicated; we'll prioritize since you have a Q3 availability need.
[21:25] Priya: ok please include compliance SLA language for Dedicated in the docs.

[23:00] (closing)
[23:10] Jamie: thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet.
[23:20] Sofia: thanks everyone.
[23:25] meeting end
next_steps: Jamie Patel: send granular usage & per-route cost breakdown by 2025-05-12
Marcus Li: share rollout/canary best practices, trace integration snippet within 3 business days
Jamie Patel: provide Dedicated pilot cost estimate and proposed routing plan by 2025-05-15
Security: send SOC2 and KMS integration guides (attach under NDA)
action_items: Jamie Patel: send granular usage & per-route cost breakdown - due 2025-05-12
Marcus Li: share rollout/canary best practices and trace snippet - due 2025-05-11
Engineering: implement cache pre-warm hook for nightly embeddings - due 2025-05-14
Jamie Patel: prepare Dedicated pilot contract terms and compliance addendum - due 2025-05-15
